_about: THE PRESETS OF THE PROCESSED RETURN (PLAN 10.8; DEC-21 · 21b · 22; RUNNING_LOG §116) — the transformations a return brick may give its sample: ONE effect of the engine's chain under a short envelope. A return's variant is  <key>-<envelope>  and its sample is  <sample>~<key>-<envelope>  (bfl-impulse-1~crush4-perc), rendered by the engine right after the sample's capture. Read by the composer page (electronics/score/le_objects.js, opts.presetsUrl) and by tools/deal_variants.js. `args` are the chain's own control names (electronics/sc/process.scd), whole — nothing is merged in; a value may be a RANGE [lo, hi], drawn fresh each time the plan is sent. Rows 1 … 7 are the shelf's (bank/candidates.json, `from`): the shelf keeps what he heard, this file what a return can use under ~0.4 … 0.7 s, and `changed` says the difference. Rows 8 … 21 are the AI's, PROVISIONAL until his ear.

colour.what: the effect is in the attack: the variant is as long as the impulse itself

time.what: the effect needs room: one and three quarters of the impulse

perc.what: 3 ms up, the rest down (Env.perc): keeps the attack

expodec.what: instant, then an exponential fall: keeps the attack

gauss.what: a bell: the attack is gone, a swell

tri.what: a triangle: up to the middle, then down

tail.what: the ring version — no envelope: it rings out to −60 dB under its peak, or is cut and faded at a RING TIME drawn fresh at every plan send, between 950 and 1350 ms past the source (his word 2026-10-05, RUNNING_LOG §118). A [lo, hi] here is drawn like a dial's range

presets.name: freeze — the spectrum held
presets.changed: caught at 60 ms, not 130 — under a ~0.7 s envelope it must speak at once; the shelf's cap (1200) gave way to the tail envelope's ring time (§118)

presets.name: JPverb — a bright room
presets.changed: mix 0.85, not 0.6 — the room has to be heard inside the envelope; the shelf's cap (1100) gave way to the tail envelope's ring time (§118)

presets.name: feedback — the bloom, six strings
presets.changed: bloom 0.15 s, not 3 s (a 3 s bloom is silent under ~0.7 s); its strings and tone kept; the peak matched to the source's (his was not: it would land 9 dB hotter with a fast bloom); the shelf's cap (1700) gave way to the tail envelope's ring time (§118)

presets.name: buffer override — a pitch at 200 Hz
tape — half speed, an octave down
